Jude Bellingham scores 'the best goal of my life' as his stunning long-range volley helps Real Madrid come from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 18:45 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:20 EST, 25 November 2026.
  • Jude Bellingham underlined his class once more with a stunning goal as Real Madrid came from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1.
  • With Real trailing 1-0 at half-time, the England superstar - who started as a substitute to rest - was one of three changes made by Jose Mourinho and his impact was felt 15 minutes later in an emphatic style.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 18:45 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:20 EST, 25 November 2026.

Jude Bellingham underlined his class once more with a stunning goal as Real Madrid came from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1.

With Real trailing 1-0 at half-time, the England superstar - who started as a substitute to rest - was one of three changes made by Jose Mourinho and his impact was felt 15 minutes later in an emphatic style.

Collecting a loose ball from around 25 yards outside the box, Bellingham controlled it with his left foot, before flicking it up with his right foot and volleying it with the outside of that boot into the far corner of the PSV goal. The pace and precision of the strike was breathtaking as it flew past Matej Kovar and hit the inside of the post before going in.

It was a strike that was befitting of any match, and it proved to be the decisive one as that made it 2-1 to the hosts before they later ran riot.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked that finish, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.'.

He later elaborated to TNT Sports about his goal: 'They're [his goals] normally a lot closer, aren't they,' he joked.

SENSATIONAL JUDE BELLINGHAM 🤯Bellingham gives the hosts the lead with a magnificent volley 🔥 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/WdP6ULx8wE.

Jude Bellingham (right) scored a stunning volley to inspire Real Madrid to beat PSV Eindhoven.

Bellingham came off the bench to put Real ahead with this beautiful right-footed volley.

PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar could only watch on as the ball flew past him and go into the net.

'That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and I just thought I'd hit it with the outside of my boot.

'I'm not one for smashing the ball too hard and it was a nice moment and important for the win as well.'.

Bellingham's performance, he also set up Vinicius Jr for the fifth goal, was acknowledged by Mourinho and Real captain Fede Valverde, who scored their equaliser, post-match too.

'Obviously Jude is a different type of player and he gave us what we didn't have in the first half,' Mourinho said. 'He changed the game, scored an incredible goal.'.

Valverde concurred declaring: 'He did well. We were struggling to keep the ball behind their midfielders and when Jude came in he gave us that tranquillity to control possession.'.

The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported that the 23-year-old is in advance talks over a fresh Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Talks were initiated in September over an extension until 2031 and have been progressing well since with sources at Madrid confident they are close to reaching a conclusion.

Bellingham is in advance contract talks with Real Madrid over signing an extension until 2031.

Bellingham is expected to be handed improved terms to put him on par with team-mate Vinicius Jr, who agreed a fresh deal last summer reputedly on around £500,000 a week after tax.

As for Tuesday's win over PSV, Real are now top of the Champions League league phase standings after maintaining their 100 per cent record in the competition this season with a fifth-straight win.

According to recent reports, 1. Erling Haaland, Manchester City: £510,000 per week.

2. Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid: £503,000 per week.

3. Vinicius Jr, Real Madrid: £500,000 per week.

Sources indicate that 4. Harry Kane, Bayern Munich: £402,000 per week.

5. Virgil van Dijk, Liverpool: £350,000 per week.

However, they didn't have it all their own way as PSV took a deserved lead in the 32nd minute from the penalty spot, with 37-year-old captain Ivan Perisic showing all his experience, ignoring the whistles ringing out around the Bernabeu before sending Thibaut Courtois the wrong way.

They almost doubled their lead before the break as the unmarked Kodai Sano glanced a header off target as the visitors continued to cause Real serious problems.

Real equalised five minutes after the break, thanks to Arda Guler's quick-thinking, with the Turkish midfielder flicking a backheeled pass to Valverde in the area, who steered his first-time shot into the bottom corner.

Real's fans were on their feet 10 minutes later, scarcely believing what they had seen, while Bellingham's team-mates looked similarly shell-shocked.

Marc Cucurella walked away with his head in his hands in wonder while the other Real players rushed to congratulate the scorer.

Real took command after Bellingham's goal and punished a loose pass in the PSV defence, Guler finding the unmarked Mbappe to extend the France forward's scoring run to seven successive Champions League appearances.

Mbappe added his second before Vinicius rounded off a resounding victory from Bellingham's pass, underlining the Spanish side's credentials as serious contenders to take Paris Saint-Germain's crown.

Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1068 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, this time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal.
  • But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.
  • It has been revealed that as a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, this time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal. More than 80 countries backed the idea.

But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.

It has been revealed that as a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap. At the same time, a group of 57 countries frustrated with the deadlock at the consensus-based UN talks decided to form a "coalition of the willing" to accelerate the fossil fuel exit outside the COP framework.

They held their own summit in April in Santa Marta, Colombia — the first such conference to specifically focus on implementing the transition away from fossil fuels (referred to as TAFF).

Co-hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands, the Santa Marta conference brought together countries including Canada, Norway, Brazil, Nigeria, Mexico, Australia and Germany, as well as highly climate-vulnerable states such as Vanuatu.

The idea was for governments to start developing national roadmaps and working out how to restructure their financial and trade systems to wean themselves off polluting energy sources — an incredibly complicated undertaking, particularly for developing countries dependent on revenue from fossil fuel exports.

Part of their discussions focused on cutting subsidies for oil, coal and gas, as well as supporting people whose livelihoods rely on the fossil fuel industry to find new forms of income.

A little over six months on from the Santa Marta meeting, representatives from almost 200 countries are holding talks in Antalya, Turkey, as part of the latest UN climate conference.

Countries agreed for the first time in 2023 to transition away from fossil fuels — the main driver behind rising global temperatures. But summits since then have failed to pin down how to implement that pledge.

It's not yet clear whether the Santa Marta coalition will influence ambition at this year's COP.

"I think it's more of a long-term game," said Chetna Hareesh Kumar, a climate policy analyst at the Berlin-based research organization NewClimate Institute.

Industry observers note that she says it's too soon to expect the coalition to have an influence on the negotiations but adds that that could change at future COPs. The grouping could bring more nations on board if, for example, it indicates it can be truly inclusive, address the needs of different types of countries and show that a transition is feasible.

One role the group is playing, according to Alexandra Scott, a senior climate diplomacy adviser at Italian climate change think tank ECCO, is "keeping up the political momentum," and showing "that there is this huge group of countries who really want to accelerate this transition away from fossil fuels.".

She says it's also building an invaluable "cadre of knowledge" on how to develop national TAFF intends and deal with barriers individual countries face — like how to secure funding for the infrastructure investments needed for the energy transition.

The Santa Marta group is "really answering a lot of the questions that countries have always had on how on earth do we even start to transition our whole economy off fossil fuels?" Scott stated.

This expertise being shared and tested in practice can show what such a transformation could look like and the knowledge brought into COP, added Scott.

Industry observers note that since the Santa Marta conference, Germany, France and the Netherlands have released national plans to phase out fossil fuels. While the plans contain no newly introduced commitments, experts see them as a positive first step.

Industry observers note that kumar states more countries could announce similar plans just ahead of the second TAFF summit in Tuvalu next year. Finland presented its TAFF roadmap in the first week of COP, but analysts do not expect many more countries to follow suit soon.

Another potential boost that could get momentum going is Brazil's recently published global roadmap to transition away from fossil fuels, promised at last year's COP.

Sources indicate that the nearly 200-page document seeks to serve as a toolkit for countries shifting from fossil fuels to renewable energy, such as wind and solar. It envisages countries making a phased transition between 2028 and 2033.

The aim, Ana Toni, CEO of last year's COP, told AP, is to break down the transition into "smaller actionable solutions" and help countries make practical progress.

The roadmap suggests measures tailored to each country's circumstances, including dependence on fossil fuel and financial capacities. "Levers" it proposes include reducing fossil fuel subsidies, expanding renewable energy and cutting methane emissions.

Recent findings suggest that kumar called it a "customizable" approach that allows every country to take action, regardless of its situation. "The question really is now what countries do with it and how much momentum they can generate," she added.

This year's climate change summit in Turkey — taking place after a series of deadly heat waves in Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that killed more than 1,400 people — isn't expected to result in any substantial announcements about fossil fuels.

Global renewable energy capacity has surged in recent years, making up a third of the world's power generation for the first time in 2025. But many countries still rely on coal, oil and gas.

A database compiled by the German environmental organization Urgewald reveals that most oil and gas companies worldwide, among them QatarEnergy, Saudi Aramco and Russia's Gazprom, are exploring or developing new reserves.

Meanwhile, subsidies for fossil fuels amount to around $920 billion (around €830 billion) per year, according to data from the OECD, but that number is falling.

Industry observers note that one issue Turkey is pushing at the COP conference is electrification. It's calling on countries to endorse the goal of 35% of final energy consumption coming from electricity by 2035 — up from around 20% today.

The pledge has drawn criticism from some circles, though, for leaving open whether that additional electricity needs to come from clean sources.

Ideally, Kumar remarked, electrification would be powered by renewables and tied to a goal of phasing out polluting fossil fuels.

"If something like that could make it to the final text, that would be a really good sign for momentum.".

Pep Guardiola defended Carlo Ancelotti during an interview with Brazil legend Romario, explaining to his former Barcelona teammate why he should be patient with the Italian tactician: ‘How many World Cups has Brazil played?’.

Romario has been one of Ancelotti’s harshest critics, especially after the Seleçao’s elimination from the 2026 World Cup Round of 16.

Guardiola has faced Ancelotti’s teams many times and clearly doesn’t share his former Barcelona teammate’s view.

It has been revealed that “How many World Cups has Brazil played? Million! You’ve lost more than you’ve won,” Guardiola noted.

Romario argued that he’s not annoyed that Brazil don’t win, but by the way they play.

Sources indicate that “I’ve coached Brazilian players, and everyone claims the pressure here is greater than anywhere else. It’s very hard,” Guardiola replied.

In a recent development, “I know Carlo a bit. I’ve played against him many times; he’s beaten me a million times. He’s an extraordinary person, and I have no doubt about his ability. He’s come to a upcoming country, to a new culture, and sometimes you need a bit more time. You know there isn’t enough time to train a national team. We’ll see what happens.

In a recent development, “[It happens to] most of the coaches who go from a club to a national team for the first time. I believe that, in the end, football is football; you have less time and have to adapt, but I’m sorry, Mario, I couldn’t doubt Carlo’s ability; it’s impossible, impossible. I know him. People say, ‘He’s good at managing the group’; everyone notes he’s the best. I faced him, and he’s very smart. He makes tactical decisions. He knows, as I do, that if you don’t win, you won’t last. Why did I stay at Manchester City for so many years? Because we won a lot. If not, you go home.”.

Romario and Guardiola also spoke about their defeat in the 1994 Champions League Final against Fabio Capello’s Milan.

Romario asked Pep whether that Milan side were technically stronger than their Barcelona, but Pep seemed unsure.

“They were very strong, very, very strong. We were too, but they were really strong,” he said.

“It’s very hard with Italian football. Capello had his way of playing, different from Johan’s [Cruijff], but they were a top side.”.

In the same interview, Guardiola spoke for the first time about rejecting an offer to coach Italy’s national team last summer, saying he needed to rest and admitting he could have accepted the proposal if it had come at a different time in his life.

Espanyol beat Athletic Club 1-0 in Bilbao through a Roberto Fernández goal. The result extends a strong run since Manolo González left and leaves Athletic seventh after a home defeat in which they dominated the statistics.

A crowd of 46,107 was at San Mamés on Friday 20 November 2026. The fixture opened Matchday 13 of LaLiga EA Sports.

Recent findings suggest that the win was Eder Sarabia’s second in charge of Espanyol and his second in a row away from home. The club have now taken seven of the nine points available since González left, according to EFE. Espanyol named Sarabia head coach on 28 October 2026, on a contract that runs until 2028.

According to recent reports, his appointment followed a 4-3 Copa del Rey defeat at Sestao River. A 1-0 win at Villarreal, a 0-0 draw with Deportivo La Coruna and Friday’s victory in Bilbao make up Espanyol’s results since González’s exit. Their goal difference now stands at zero.

According to recent reports, the first half ended goalless. Tyrhys Dolan replaced Pere Milla in the 57th minute. Sarabia also sent on Gabriel Moscardó and Javi Hernández in the 65th minute.

It has been revealed that A minute later, Dolan set up Fernández for the winner. It was the striker’s sixth league goal of the season, putting him eighth in the LaLiga scoring list. He finished with 3 shots and a rating of 7.92.

Sarabia then brought on Unai Núñez and Javi Puado in the 84th minute to protect the lead. Clemens Riedel was booked in the third minute of stoppage time, Espanyol’s only card of the night.

Goalkeeper Ángel Fortuño made six saves to keep a clean sheet.

It has been revealed that the result gave Espanyol a third successive league win over Athletic. They won 2-0 at home on 13 May 2026 and 2-1 at San Mamés on 22 December 2025.

Sources indicate that athletic controlled most of the statistics. They had 58% of possession and 9 corners to Espanyol’s 2. On target, the hosts had 6 efforts and the visitors 3.

Edin Terzić moved away from the 4-4-2 he had used in previous matches to fit Oihan Sancet into a 4-2-3-1. The change did not produce more attacking threat. Deia judged this to be Athletic’s worst performance at San Mamés since Terzić took charge.

Nico Williams had 5 shots and 3 key passes. Iñigo Ruiz de Galarreta also created 3 chances in 29 minutes on the pitch. Athletic collected three yellow cards, for Iñaki Williams, Ruiz de Galarreta and Yeray Álvarez.

Athletic fall to defeat at San Mames.#AthleticEspanyol #AthleticClub 🦁 pic.twitter.com/tRnTpjuX14.

Before kick-off, San Mamés paid tribute to Elene Gurtubay and Daniela Agote, who won the Under-20 World Cup.

After 12 matches, Terzić’s side have 16 points. Their recent run reads one draw, two wins and one defeat in the league before Friday’s loss. Real Sociedad sit fifth on 22 points.

Athletic travel to bottom side Malaga on Saturday 28 November. Espanyol host Getafe on Monday 30 November.

Industry observers note that we'll be back with the latest headlines out of Germany tomorrow. Bis dann!

Germany dominated neighbor and historic rival the Netherlands in their Nations League quarterfinal match-up at Berlin's Olympic Stadium on Monday evening.

It was the team's sixth game under head coach Jürgen Klopp and the 50th ever between the two sides.

Germany's 5-0 shellacking of the Oranje was their most lopsided victory since 1959, when they won 7-0. In all, Germany have now won 19 of those matches, the Netherlands have won 12, and 18 ended in a draw.

It has been revealed that speaking to German broadcaster ARD after the game, attacking midfielder Florian Wirtz — who scored twice in the fixture — said: "We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second half.".

Despite the loss, Xavi Hernandez's Dutch side will reach the final eight alongside Germany.

Prior to the match, Klopp had made it clear that he and his team were approaching Monday's showdown as a final after having lost to Greece 1-0 in his first home game in the job on September 27.

By night's end, Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck each scored once and Brajan Gruda scored once and added two assists on top of Wirtz's double.

Klopp has been high on Wirtz, who has come under fire for not delivering at Liverpool since his arrival there in June 2025, and his bet seems to be paying off with the 23-year-old now scoring four goals in his last four games for Germany.

According to recent reports, "We don't care who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly," said Wirtz on Monday evening before adding: "We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we've taken some great steps in our development as a team.".

A group of five EU member states, including Germany, have entered talks over a scheme to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda.

The plan to set up so-called return hubs in a non-EU country had been declared by the group — which also includes Austria, the Netherlands, Greece and Denmark — had first been announced back in September.

Tesla has earmarked some €3 billion ($3.3 billion) to expand its factory in Germany, near to Berlin.

The Grünheide complex will be expanded to start producing the electric car firm's driverless Cybercabs, with output expected to eventually reach 1 million units.

The Elon Musk-owned company noted construction would begin in 2027, with the first Cybercabs rolling off the line in 2029.

"With this, we are laying the foundations for the world's most technologically advanced Tesla factory here in Grünheide," Tesla mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.

Matt Pearson on our sports desk breaks down where the power struggle currently stands, with the deadline for candiates just a matter of hours away now.

Lawmakers in the state parliament in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania have voted in Manuela Schwesig for another term as state premier.

The 52-year-old has been in the role since 2017 and is heading into a third term.

The vote was a secret ballot, but it can still be assumed who voted and how.

She received 39 of the 68 votes cast in the chamber, exactly as many as commanded by Schwesig's three-party coaliton of her Social Democrats (29), the ecologist Greens (5), and the socialist Left Party (5).

While Söder's comments in Munich focused in particular on the policy the coalition in Berlin had not delivered, Merz initiatlly focused on talking up the efficacy of his federal coalition.

"We are aware of the situation. We know that we now need to deliver. And we also know that we face difficult talks within the coalition. But I would also say from the experiences of the last weeks that there are solutions to the problems which we have in Germany," Merz mentioned.

Merz said that in the 18 months since last year's election, the coalition "has already successfully implemented many things, not 'set them into motion' as people like to say, but actually implemented.".

He noted a total of 17 bills going through the second and third reading process in the lower house of parliament, the Bundestag, last week, "including the most comprehensive reforms of our intelligence and security services that we have ever done in [post-war] Germany.".

Among others, he thanked Bavarian Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, a senior member of the Bavarian CSU sister party to Merz's own conservative CDU, for his contribution to this.

Merz also touted the support given to CSU politician Ilse Aigner, not just from his CDU but from the Social Democrat coalition partners and the Greens, to become the next president, calling her a person who would "represent our country very well at home and abroad.".

After hailing these accomplishments, Merz then turned to electricity tax cuts, saying he anticipated talks on the matter on Tuesday that would be "very short.".

He said that over the weekend, coalition leaders had revisited the figures, and now believed they would be able to "completely" reduce electricity taxes to the minimum European levels in 2027 "also for private households.".

Bavarian state premier Markus Söder has appeared with Friedrich Merz at a press conference during the chancellor's trip to Munich.

It seems Söder, Merz and the CDU/CSU believe they have unfinished business after the budget was finalized in the Bundestag late last week.

Merz had pledged in the run-up to the decision to provide a reduction in electricity tax for all, but the final agreement did not include this step, with the coalition partners the Social Democrats (SPD) saying it was not adequately costed.

Söder stated he and Merz had discussed "backup for the coming days," for Berlin and for a "collective stance, that is really, really notable.".

He said the coming days were about "demonstrating credibility in politics," seemingly in reference to Merz's promise that the coalition did not ultimately deliver.

"That's why it's really important to us that we do indeed bring about the reduction in electricity tax," Söder noted. "This is important for businesses. It would be a relief for citizens. But it's also a matter of credibility and it's written in the coalition agreement.".

Söder said that as to the question of "where the money comes from, with a €560 billion (roughly $615 billion) budget, with €200 billion in upcoming debt, nobody can tell me there's no potential within the budgeting process.".

A festive piece of merchandise on the right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) "fan shop" website has upset some religious leaders in Germany.

Called a "chocolate Nicholas," it appears to depict a semblance of Saint Nicholas in bishop's regalia and the party's colors and holding a book with "AfD" written on the cover where a Bible might be in more traditional iconography.

The Bishop of Essen, Franz-Josef Overbeck, was highly critical of the promotion in Monday's edition of the Bild newspaper.

"The AfD is appropriating Christian symbols for party campaigning," Overbeck said. "Showing the holy Nicholas in a blue coat with mitre, staff and the gospel with an AfD logo is not in order.".

Overbeck acknowledged that other organizations like football clubs would sell chocolate Christmas figurines in club colors, but he said they would tend to refrain from including overtly Christian symbols when doing so.

Bild quoted an AfD spokesman as saying that as a "liberal-conservative party that clearly associates itself with Christian values," the item fit "particularly well" with the party image.

The main German protestant church group EKD's cultural representative, Johann Hinrich Claussen, remarked the offer revealed the AfD had "no understanding of traditions and no respect" for Christianity.

He described the action as "embarrassing and revealing," and mentioned that Christianity was "supra-partisan.".

According to recent reports, "The AfD knows little about what is holy to Christians. Otherwise, it would be aware that Bishop Nicholas of Myra, in what today is Demre in Turkey, stood clearly for uniting the occident and the orient. Beyond that, he is the patron saint of rescues at sea," Claussen remarked.

The partner of deceased Bavarian politician Hubert Aiwanger has said that anybody is welcome at his funeral this coming Saturday.

Aiwanger was the economy minister in Bavaria's state government as the leader of the junior coalition partners to the center-right CSU.

"Hubert was a man of the people and so it stands to reason that anyone who liked or treaasured him is allowed to come to his funeral," Tanja Schweiger wrote on her Instagram profile overnight.

In a recent development, she was posting after a requiem in the state capital Munich paying tribute to the leader of the Free Voters (Freie Wähler) party over the weekend. Around 1,100 people attended this ceremony.

Aiwanger died suddenly and unexpectedly on November 4 during a working visit to Berlin, aged 55.

Prosecutors have since stated he died of natural causes, after he was found dead in his hotel room.

Germany's national men's football team will play neighbors and rivals the Netherlands for the 50th time on Monday night.

And there's quite a lot at stake for Jürgen Klopp's team in the last group stage game of the Nations League competition at Berlin's Olympiastadion.

If Germany win, they will qualify for the knockout stages, but a defeat could lead to potential relegation into the second tier of Nations League football.

Klopp was upbeat in the pre-match press conference at the prospect of playing the Netherlands, who he noted play "Xavi football," in the image of the skillful Spanish playmaker and World Cup winner coaching the team.

According to recent reports, "I've always loved playing against teams like this. For all my coaching career," Klopp remarked. "When someone states, 'hey they can really play football,' then in my mind the party's already started.".

Recent findings suggest that A full house with some 71,000 fans is expected in the capital when the game kicks off. Klopp played on the Dutch reputation for liberal use of bicylces in his comments to reporters, saying he wanted to "put a stick in their spokes" and dislodge them from the saddle.

The notion of a bridge over the valley between Ratingen and Heiligenhaus to the east of Düsseldorf in western Germany as part of the A44 highway is more than half a century old. And the physical bridge itself has stood, complete, ever since 2022.

Yet still the crossing is not connected to any roads at either end.

A construction project to build the last 4.4 kilometers of highway and link the bridge to the A44 highway will formally start on Monday.

State premier Hendrik Wüst, as well as the regional transport and traffic ministers will attend the ground-breaking ceremony.

A project first conceived some 55 years ago has faced repeated delays because of lawsuits, environmental protection studies and onerous planning and permit procedures.

According to recent reports, the bridge across the Angerbachtal (Angerbach Valley) should improve the road connection between the North Rhine-Westphalia state capital of Düsseldorf, the Bergisches Land mountain range and the industrial cities in the Ruhr Valley. It's also meant to help remove some strain from the perenially busy A3 highway and to improve the road connections to Düsseldorf International Airport.

The last stretch of highway is expected to cost around €200 million (roughly $220 million), or roughly the annual costs incurred each year by forcing traffic to divert around it, according to estimates from Düsseldorf's IHK industry and trade association.

Construction is expected to take several years, no formal end date has yet been set.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz heads to Munich early on Monday, for a meeting with the leadership of the Bavarian Christian Social Democrats (CSU), the sister party to his conservative  Christian Democrats(CDU).

No concrete details about the talks were made public ahead of time, except for the CSU saying it would serve as a general exchange that had been planned for some time.

The trip comes a week after Merz nominated Ilse Aigner as the next German president, likely paving the way for her to become the first woman and first CSU politician to assume the role.

It also follows soon after the 2027 federal budget cleared a marathon meeting of the parliamentary budget committee in Berlin. This serves as one of the more conspicuous examples of the frictions and difficulties in the grand coalition between the Christian Democrats and the center-left Social Democrats — with the compromises it contains a point of frustration among the CSU and for state premier Markus Söder.

The northeastern state parliament in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania will likely vote in Social Democrat (SPD) Manuela Schwesig for another term as state premier early in the afternoon.

The 52-year-old, who first stepped into the role in 2017, prepares to lead a new coalition of the SPD, the environmentalist Greens and the socialist Left Party after state elections in September.

The right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) emerged as the largest single party in the sparsely populated state.

But still, the political calculus that emerged was arguably simpler than in Berlin — where the socialist Left Party is the largest party but could struggle to lead a coaltion — and in Saxony-Anhalt, where the AfD was by far the largest party but short of an outright majority.

Schwesig's SPD claimed 29 seats, with the Greens and the Left each taking 5, meaning that when combined, they hold a fairly clear majority over the AfD with its 32 seats.

The SPD's relatively successful performance in the state, at least compared to its national struggles, has also led to Schwesig being linked with a possible return to federal politics. The SPD prepares to elect a latest leadership duo early next year.

Schwesig has already had a spell in Berlin as the federal minsiter for families, pensioners and women, and briefly led the SPD on an interim basis in 2017, but after this she returned to her home state to seek the top regional job instead.

#118107. Blend public cash and private innovation to unlock drug development

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1782 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Blend public cash and private innovation to unlock drug development

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1782 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fresh model of research and development is needed to incentivize manufacturers to go after diseases that aren’t sure bets.Credit: Stanislav Gvozd/Getty.
  • According to recent reports, for decades, most countries have followed the same model of biomedical innovation.
  • In a recent development, this approach has generated extraordinary drugs and therapies as well as economic success.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh model of research and development is needed to incentivize manufacturers to go after diseases that aren’t sure bets.Credit: Stanislav Gvozd/Getty.

According to recent reports, for decades, most countries have followed the same model of biomedical innovation. Basic research is undertaken mostly by universities and academia, and private industry leads the translation of research into health solutions1.

In a recent development, this approach has generated extraordinary drugs and therapies as well as economic success. In 2022, the pharmaceutical sector contributed US$2.3 trillion — or around 1.7% — to global gross domestic product (GDP) and supported 75 million jobs2.

How tech billionaires are disrupting biomedical science.

How tech billionaires are disrupting biomedical science.

It has been revealed that however, market failures have been common. Companies have underinvested in developing therapeutics for common diseases with poorly understood biological mechanisms, such as depression, anxiety and kidney disease, because they consider them too commercially risky or unprofitable to pursue3.

In a recent development, to address this gap, we propose an adapted innovation model based on mission-driven public–private partnerships (PPPs), in which government acts as a leading strategic investor. By bringing together the best scientists in academia and industry and lowering risks in industry development in areas of public need and for diseases with limited understanding, this model would accelerate translation, advance health and increase economic returns.

Here, we outline how it would work. It will require systems to ensure affordable access to drugs and therapies, as well as revenue sharing between public and private partners to guarantee public benefits and to support investments in innovation.

Recent findings suggest that complex diseases that affect swathes of the population create persistent health and economic burdens. Yet, the current biomedical innovation model has proved limited in addressing evolving health needs. Because private investment is guided by assessments of risk and return, it tends to favour diseases with well-defined biological mechanisms and high commercial potential. Diseases that are biologically complex, varied or associated with uncertain markets remain underexplored.

It has been revealed that for example, in 2023, more than 300 million people globally had depression. The condition will cost the global economy an estimated $12 trillion between 2025 and 20504. In the United States in 2024, one in five people reported that they had received a diagnosis of major depressive disorder during their lifetime, resulting in an economic burden of $334 billion annually across health-care, household-related and workforce costs5. Yet, the leading drug class for depression (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) has remained unchanged since the 1970s6.

The grand strategy to transform psychiatry — by personalizing mental-health care.

The grand initiative to transform psychiatry — by personalizing mental-health care.

Industry observers note that other chronic diseases impose similarly large burdens. For example, chronic kidney disease affects around 800 million people worldwide — nearly one in seven — and is projected to become the fifth leading cause of death globally by 2040 if current trends continue7,8. Yet, existing therapies cannot stem its toll on human lives.

It has been revealed that antimicrobial resistance is another example, which is associated with 4.7 million deaths globally each year and could contribute to 10 million deaths annually by 2050. Increased treatment costs for people with resistant infections amount to $1 trillion every year9. The antibiotic development pipeline has been depleted over time as economic factors render companies’ return on investment lower than that for other drug classes9. These factors include insufficient funding for research and challenging business models, given the short duration of antibiotic treatments and the need to reserve successful latest antibiotics as drugs of last resort, to be used after all other options have failed.

According to recent reports, bringing a therapy to market from discovery can take 10–15 years and cost anywhere between $880 million and $2.3 billion10,11. The majority (90%) of drug candidates fail after entering clinical studies, clinical trials and drug-approval processes12. And companies won’t invest if they are unsure whether a drug will be profitable.

Consequently, many diseases and conditions have no or few available therapies or only modestly effective options13. What’s needed is a mission-driven strategy to guide scientific capabilities and industry development towards areas of public need by elucidating biological mechanisms and aligning incentives for diseases in which market forces alone are insufficient14.

We propose addressing this misalignment of incentives by reconceptualizing the government’s role in therapeutic advancement through a model of mission-driven PPP. Complementing existing grant-based systems, the model would position the government as a principal investor in select areas of therapeutic development.

Industry observers note that the government would thus influence which areas of health and science receive concentrated attention and how successful outcomes are deployed for the public good. Such a model could address specific national needs and global challenges. Here are seven components.

Technicians at work in a pharmaceutical factory.Credit: Getty.

Select disease targets. We propose the establishment of a government-appointed independent advisory body or commission tasked with identifying priority disease targets using transparent, evidence-based criteria, including disease burden, economic cost, scientific readiness and demonstrable market failure. Further criteria to gauge and consider public input into the selection process could be implemented to ensure public trust.

Set up collaborations. A national government, acting alone or as part of an international consortium, would assume a leading role in supporting basic research into biological mechanisms. It would do so by bringing together basic scientists from academia and translational experts from industry to reduce risks in translational development. Private industry would contribute expertise in drug development, clinical trials, regulatory strategy, manufacturing and commercialization.

Provide initial investments. The proposed PPP would not replace existing grant-based systems or market-driven innovation; rather, it would act as a complement by targeting disease areas in which market risks and incentives consistently fail to generate sufficient private investment. The approach could yield fresh therapies and reduce the cost of care to society while generating revenue from new products.

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

In the United States, we propose a federal investment of one billion dollars annually over ten years, directed to specific disease areas. That is less than 1.8% of total US government spending on biomedical research, which was $54.5 billion in 2024. This would be supplemented by smaller investments of 10–20% of one billion dollars from a consortium of philanthropic foundations and industry partners joining the initiative in response to a request for application. Given the high costs of bringing a new drug to market, a $10-billion total investment should provide the scale and time needed to pursue about three major disease targets10–12.

Feed revenues back in. Public return is a defining feature of the PPP. Existing biomedical funding structures are mainly grant making, with the implication that public benefit will emerge indirectly through the downstream health improvements and economic growth spurred by discovery. By contrast, this PPP framework would directly incorporate public accountability as well as returns.

It has been revealed that the government would need to leverage its status as a majority investor to ensure access, fair pricing and affordability. It might require conditions such as agreements to ensure access. Pricing frameworks could incorporate a value-based approach to pricing, in which health insurers offer reimbursements determined by a drug’s value for patients. Affordability conditions, such as reasonable-pricing clauses, would also serve as powerful leverage.

If they play together, it will be the first time brothers have represented England in the same team since Gary and Phil Neville 19 years ago.

This time last year, Tuchel cast doubt over Jude’s place in his team by picking Morgan Rogers over him, having not included the Real Madrid midfielder in an England squad the previous month.

Recent findings suggest that but Jude performed superbly for Tuchel at the World Cup and was England’s best player during the last international camp. Tuchel revealed he has listened to his advice by calling up 21-year-old Jobe.

Asked if his relationship with Jude has developed, Tuchel said: “It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course, but we are in a good place.

According to recent reports, “I love to be his coach, he’s a top player, a very influential player and it goes both ways. If Jude was not feeling comfortable, he would not perform at that level.

“At the moment, you see he’s happy to come into camp, he’s happy with the role he has, he’s fully invested and now to have the chance to have both of them [Bellingham brothers] is just the next step. I hope we have finished with the down. You never know as a coach.”.

Jobe has captained England’s Under-21s and, as well as U21 head coach Lee Carlsey, Tuchel acknowledged the influence of Jude on the Borussia Dortmund midfielder’s first senior call.

Jude once said that playing with Jobe for England would be “the biggest dream of my life” and that it would mean more to him than any trophies.

Discussing Jude’s influence on Jobe’s selection, Tuchel said: “We spoke about his brother because I was aware it was always his dream and Jude was always like, ‘Watch him, he’s good, he can make it,’ I would say, ‘Yeah we are watching him.’ And we know, of course, from Lee Carsley and we see him with the Under-21s and there is such positive feedback.

“This is also the signal that if you are good in the Under-21s, this is the next step. We had it with Elliot Anderson, we had it with Alex Scott, we have it with Jarell Quansah and it counts. If you play good for England in the Under-19s, 20s, 21s, if you play good for England in tournaments then it means something.”.

In a recent development, tuchel at one point had to correct himself, with a laugh, when he accidentally referred to Jobe as Jube. On the subject of how Jobe reacted to his call-up and the comparisons with his brother that he will inevitably face, Tuchel remarked: “He has to live with this that everyone will compare them. They look similar, even in their movements, but they are very different players. And let’s see – they are also different characters, at least that’s what I heard.

In a recent development, “He [Jobe] watched training very early in my [reign]. In my first March camp maybe, he came over and watched his brother train. We chatted and we remarked, ‘Ah, it would be nice if one day you are with him [Jude].’ He was very kind and polite and I’m glad to have him in camp.

“He couldn’t stop smiling [when I told him]. He has the same beautiful smile as Jude, so it’s nice to have him. Let’s see what the effect is. What I saw, Jude was always the significant brother that you imagine, taking care of his younger brother and making sure everything is alright. Behaving like a big brother. And that helps Jobe now. And it will be beautiful for Jude to have his brother close and in camp and to have this experience together. It’s a very special moment for them.”.

According to recent reports, for his club, Bellingham is far more than just a midfielder. He is also a figurehead and a driving force behind the club’s marketing activities. The Bellingham name, made famous by his brother Jude, who played for Dortmund from 2020 to 2023 before moving to Real Madrid for almost €130m (£108m), is arguably the most recognisable in Dortmund’s squad. When the club embarked on a marketing tour of Asia last summer, Bellingham was front and centre. At a Puma event in Osaka, he addressed the guests. In Tokyo, where the Dortmund delegation travelled next, a film about BVB was projected on to a huge skyscraper. The central figure: Jobe Bellingham. And after the public training sessions, Japanese supporters were particularly eager to get photos with him.

Jobe never wanted to be a carbon copy of his brother. He wanted to write his own story. The club, too, has resisted direct comparisons. They just wanted Jobe, not the younger brother of a world-class star. Now the brothers will be reunited in the England squad. For Jude, it is a dream come true. He previously remarked: “We’ve played together on the streets for so long. Playing for England alongside my brother would be the greatest dream of my life. That would mean more to me than any trophy.”.

Dortmund have never fought harder for a player in recent years than Bellingham. The club’s executives first met him in person in the summer of 2020, when Jude signed. Jobe accompanied his brother to Germany. From that moment on, the club monitored every step of his development: his progress through the youth ranks at Birmingham City, the family club of the Bellinghams, and the evolution of his positioning on the pitch. After all, as a child, Jobe was still playing as a centre-forward. Over time, however, he gradually moved into deeper roles.

In May 2025, BVB decided to make their move. Word had reached Dortmund that Eintracht Frankfurt were interested and had already invited Bellingham to their training facilities. The pressure was on. Dortmund responded by pulling out all the stops. President Hans-Joachim Watzke, the man who shaped the club for more than two decades and led it to the top of German football, stepped in. He flew to England and met Bellingham face to face. It was a secret mission. Watzke was determined not to attract any attention that could jeopardise negotiations.

The problem: Sunderland, Bellingham’s former club, had secured promotion to the Premier League only a day earlier. Hundreds of supporters were gathered outside the hotel where Watzke and Bellingham were due to meet. To avoid being recognised, Watzke put on sunglasses and a cap before making his way through the crowd. He brought two gifts with him. Firstly, a BVB shirt with Jobe’s name on the back. Secondly, a handwritten note from Kovac expressing his desire to work with the midfielder. A few days later, Watzke received a phone call. It was Jobe. His decision had been made. He was joining Dortmund.

Industry observers note that ever since, the midfielder has enjoyed almost unwavering support. Watzke frequently spoke with him throughout his first season, offering encouragement and reassurance. The same was true of Kovac and other senior figures. Equally notable to his breakthrough has been team-mate Felix Nmecha, with whom Bellingham has developed a close friendship and who has become an important source of advice. When time allows, the two enjoy playing padel together. Off the pitch they are opponents; on it they form a midfield partnership.

And while his father Mark was still complaining to club officials around a year ago that his son was not getting enough playing time, the situation has changed dramatically. The Bellingham family are delighted, and his England call-up has provided further confirmation that he is on the right path.

According to recent reports, good morning and welcome to live coverage of the announcement by Thomas Tuchel of England’s squad for their remaining two Uefa Nations Group 3 matches against Croatia – them again – at Wembley next Thursday and Spain at the Metropolitano in Madrid next Sunday night. England have already qualified for the knockout phase – barring a defeat by Croatia by a margin of eight or more goals – but would need two victories to avoid France and Portugal in the next two-legged phase in March.

Tuchel’s only major injury doubt from the last squad are Arsenal’s Bukao Saka and Como’s Trevoh Chalobah as well as the more long-term absentee Tino Livramento, the man Chalobah replaced in the World Cup 26. Djed Spence has returned to full fitness and played for Inter in their Milan derby defeat last weekend while the head coach’s favourite player, Jordan Henderson, has been passed fit to play for Chelsea at his boyhood club Sunderland on Sunday though at 36 his race may finally have been run at this level despite his unexpected encore in the last 18 months.

For the first time since 2001 England will have the Ballon d’Or winner in the squad and Harry Kane will also become England’s most-capped player – barring some misfortune when Bayern Munich take on Mainz on Saturday – by leading them out at Wembley on Thursday night for his 126th appearance.

Sources indicate that whether he will be joined by Cole Palmer in the squad remains the only significant issue of note. The Chelsea forward pulled out of the last squad as part of his club’s management of his groin injury but he has played in their last four Premier League games, scoring once and being sent off once as well. Kobbie Mainoo is fit again and may be picked to see if his backside has recovered from bench splinters since his summer of exasperation.

The squad will be released at 10am and followed by Tuchel’s explanations, which we will also cover here, an hour later.

Breaking: Klopp wants Infantino out as FIFA candidate deadline looms

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (864 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has become the latest prominent football figure to call for change at the top of FIFA.
  • "Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job," he said on Sunday.
  • But with time running out before the November 18 deadline for newly introduced candidates for the presidency of world football's governing body, Infantino is looking overwhelmingly likely to win another term.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has become the latest prominent football figure to call for change at the top of FIFA.

"Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job," he said on Sunday.

But with time running out before the November 18 deadline for newly introduced candidates for the presidency of world football's governing body, Infantino is looking overwhelmingly likely to win another term.

"There are people who truly care about the future of football, people who aren't driven by financial interests," Klopp mentioned ahead of Germany's Nations League match against the Netherlands on Monday.

"If someone like that were to step up — if someone like that were to become president — I think that would be a significant improvement.".

Recent findings suggest that if that person is waiting in the wings, they're leaving it late to step on the stage. Despite a raft of federations and continental confederations, including Germany, UEFA (Europe), CONCACAF (North and Central America and the Caribbean) and AFC (Asia), calling for Infantino's head in the wake of his strategy to sell off part of the World Cup earlier this year, the incumbent appears to have stopped the bleeding.

That plan, which involved forming a subsidiary arm of FIFA called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) in order to sell off part of its commercial operations to investors including Joshua Kushner — brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner — was widely panned before being abandoned.

It followed on from widespread criticism of Infantino's awarding of a new FIFA Peace Prize to Trump, the overturning of a red card for US national team player Folarin Balogun, and with Trump's involvement, at the World Cup and a host of other controversies.

Since then, though, many public critics have backtracked amid FIFA promising to release an extra $2.7bn (€2.45bn) from its reserves over the next four years to the federations, increasing their total investment to $6.35bn.

Perhaps the most significant of these u-turns came from the AFC, who went from saying Infantino had committed a "fundamental breach of trust" in August, to offering the Swiss its "full commitment to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as the FIFA president" in October.

Sources indicate that those words were spoken by AFC President, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, who ran against Infantino when he first won the top job at FIFA in 2016. He will not run again and said that "my feeling is, I'm sure, the feeling of most of my members," in regard to Infantino.

Proof that the sentiment is not universal comes in the shape of Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japan Football Association (JFA). Tashima is one of only two people to confirm they will oppose Infantino in the March 2027 presidential elections.

It has been revealed that the 68-year-old is a well respected figure in Asian football politics and will have no problem meeting the threshold of support from five of FIFA's 211 federations. This is not like the other candidate, former Swiss international player Ramon Vega, who is an enormous outsider. Tashima appears to be running on the basis that he will be able to chart a calmer path at FIFA.

Recent findings suggest that "I am grateful that I can make this announcement with the full support of the Japan Football Association," Tashima told the Japanese newspaper Sports Nippon. "It's not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built. What FIFA needs now are these values that we have protected. I have decided to run in order to make this appeal to the world.".

But the numbers are against him. Though support from within the confederations may not be total, the backing of AFC and the African confederation (CAF) is a huge boost for Infantino, with those two alone making up 101 votes, almost enough for a majority.

In fact, the only real concern remaining for Infantino remains UEFA. The European federation, headed by Aleksander Ceferin, is a major revenue source for FIFA but the two organizations are at loggerheads. As well as a war of words, UEFA are seeking to obtain evidence for a potential Swiss criminal case against Infantino in regards to FFE. FIFA have called this a "smear campaign" and a "fishing expedition".

But, so far, UEFA has not put up a candidate. Former Arsenal coach turned FIFA Chief of Global Football Development, Arsene Wenger was thought to be a contender but has now ruled himself out. Wenger's compatriot, Philippe Diallo, has since emerged as another option, with The Guardian reporting on Monday that the French Football Federation president could be confirmed on Tuesday.

Industry observers note that while Europe is football's powerbase, particularly from a club perspective, UEFA will need Diallo, or any candidate they can convince to run, to win votes from outside its 55 nations to have any chance of success, particularly with Tashima likely to split any challenge. Even if a candidate appears before the November 18 deadline, Klopp's hope for change appears to be a long shot.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

First released in 1995, Mitreâs Ultimax ball swiftly became a defining symbol in English football. A fixture on Premier League pitches throughout the 1990s, it made history as the first football to break the 100mph speed barrier.

Now, 30 years later, Mitre has reimagined the legendary ball, bringing it back with a modern twist.

The new Ultimax Pro 30th Anniversary Ball merges the classic design with cutting-edge technology, celebrating its iconic status while setting a new standard for the next generation.

While the ball retains the familiar 6-panel construction, the classic white, blue, and red colourway, and the unmistakable crown logo, itâs been upgraded with advanced features. Hyperflow grooves reduce drag and a sleek pearl finish offers a nod to traditional 30th-anniversary gifts. The interior also sees improvements, with Hyperfoam cushioning now enhanced for cleaner strikes and even more power.

To mark the milestone, Mitre has launched the "The Next In Line" campaign, spotlighting the new wave of football talent carrying on their family legacies.

The campaign features rising stars such as Raphaella Wright-Phillips, granddaughter of Arsenal icon Ian Wright, Ruben Butt, son of Manchester United legend Nicky Butt, and Jacob Fowler, whose father is Liverpoolâs own Robbie Fowler.

The trio, each in vintage 95/96 kits, embody the connection between the past and the future â just as the fresh Ultimax Pro does itself.

Latest Update: COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1013 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • COP31 co-host Australia has kicked off the second week of climate talks in Antalya with a draft political deal calling for an "immediate transition away from fossil fuels" and a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to at least $120 billion (€109 billion).
  • Industry observers note that the goal of other co-host Turkey to increase electrification of the world's economies to 35% by 2035 also features in the text.
  • Language around a faster phaseout of oil, coal and gas is important because fossil-fuel producing nations have repeatedly pushed back against stronger wording in previous COP decisions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

COP31 co-host Australia has kicked off the second week of climate talks in Antalya with a draft political deal calling for an "immediate transition away from fossil fuels" and a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to at least $120 billion (€109 billion).

Industry observers note that the goal of other co-host Turkey to increase electrification of the world's economies to 35% by 2035 also features in the text. The draft emphasizes clean energy but notes that "electrification can provide co-benefits regardless of the electricity mix" — an approach that has proved divisive at the talks, with many insisting that electrification be strictly tied to renewable energy.

Language around a faster phaseout of oil, coal and gas is important because fossil-fuel producing nations have repeatedly pushed back against stronger wording in previous COP decisions.

"The upcoming negotiating text contains all the necessary building blocks for a successful outcome to the conference: from the goal of climate neutrality for all industrialized countries by 2030 to a work program that can keep the 1.5-degree limit in place," noted Greenpeace Germany head Martin Kaiser on Monday.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, the draft expressed "deep concern" that the 1.5 Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) temperature threshold agreed at the 2015 COP in Paris to avoid runaway climate change was now out of reach. It stressed the need for "accelerating action to minimize both the magnitude and duration of any temperature overshoot and to return global warming to below 1.5C as soon as possible.".

Recognizing a need to address rising carbon emissions, the draft highlighted efforts to "urgently and rapidly" scale up controversial technologies to capture and store CO2 to bring down atmospheric carbon levels.

Recent findings suggest that "For the first time, all the parties here are grappling with the fact that the world will inevitably exceed 1.5 degrees. Negotiators must deliver a response," said Ani Dasgupta, president of the World Resources Institute, adding that this meant going beyond slashing emissions.

"This requires scaling carbon removal through both nature-based solutions like restoring forests and wetlands, or emerging technologies that directly capture carbon from air," he told reporters.

Kaiser, however, criticized the lack of binding commitments in the draft's resolutions. He added that Europe should work with China and the most climate-vulnerable countries to keep oil-producing nations, including Russia and countries in the Middle East, from "undermining the conference's decisions and turning them into a free pass for the oil and gas industry.".

Other activists have dismissed carbon capture as a "false solution" being promoted by corporations.

Cosima Cassel, an expert at climate think tank E3G, was cautiously pleased with the draft's "ambitious language" but said it appeared the broad deal would now leave negotiators to "fight for trade-offs.".

"The test will be whether the final decision keeps the core elements once that process plays out: ambition on overshoot, defense of the science, clean electrification and forward progress on adaptation finance," she said in a statement.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Disagreements over financing largely relate to who should bear the costs of international climate action, whether financial support should be provided through grants or loans, and how funding for developing countries can be increased.

Representatives of developing nations and small island states, regions bearing the brunt of the climate crisis, have protested climate inaction and a lack of financial support in recent days.

"Climate finance isn't an extra at these talks: it's the condition for everything else," noted Rukiya Khamis, program manager for East Africa with environmental group 350.org. "It's alarming how financial pledges by wealthy, polluting countries are dropping like a stone — COP31 must stop this with a strong outcome on adaptation finance.".

"Now we must fight to keep this [adaption finance] in the final decision and ensure these promises become real, grant-based money," said Harjeet Singh of the Fill The Fund campaign, which calls on rich countries and corporations to deliver the funding needed for climate-related loss and damage, such as homes destroyed by floods and harvests ruined by drought.

"Communities are suffering devastating losses and damages today precisely because we failed to deliver adaptation at the right time," added Singh.

At 18 pages and 144 items, the draft will be the focus of lengthy discussions in the coming days as delegates try to come to an agreement by Friday. Some observers went so far as to say the document's scope was too wide to be taken seriously.

"The draft final declaration reads like a Christmas wish list," noted Niklas Höhne, a climate policy expert at the NewClimate Institute in Germany. "There are even several points on which we will obviously not be able to reach a consensus, including for example the proposal that developed countries achieve net-zero emissions by 2030.".

But Chris Bowen, chief of negotiations and Australia's minister for climate change and energy, appeared optimistic.

Sources indicate that "The general tenor and tone [of the talks] has been very constructive," he told reporters Monday. "Parties have come to me with strong views about various things, as you'd expect […] [but] they've also come in the spirit of cooperation, the spirit of respect and a spirit where parties have said to me that they want to help get an outcome.".

David Waskow, director of WRI's International Climate Initiative, said the draft text demonstrated a level of "seriousness" on important concerns like finance, electrification, oceans, overshoot scenarios and emissions of greenhouse gases including methane, which has a warming impact more than 80 times stronger than CO2.

In a recent development, "The question is whether the level of ambition on those challenges is carried through into the final outcome here," remarked Waskow. "And that's what we need to be watching closely over the coming days.".

Additional reporting by Tim Schauenberg in Antalya.

Update, November 17, 2026: This article has been updated with additional reactions to the draft text.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that substitute Carlos Espí struck late as Real Madrid came from behind to beat Celta Vigo 2-1 at the Santiago Bernabéu.
  • The victory over Celta on Saturday 21 November 2026 was Madrid’s ninth in a row.
  • The winner began with a Vinícius Júnior cross.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that substitute Carlos Espí struck late as Real Madrid came from behind to beat Celta Vigo 2-1 at the Santiago Bernabéu. The result keeps Madrid firmly in the title race with Barcelona.

The victory over Celta on Saturday 21 November 2026 was Madrid’s ninth in a row. It also kept their 100% home record this season intact.

The winner began with a Vinícius Júnior cross. Espí headed it, Celta goalkeeper Ionuț Radu saved, and the striker scored from the rebound in the six-yard box. He had been on the pitch for only a few minutes.

Espí had played only 44 minutes of LaLiga football this season before kick-off, according to ESPN. All three of his league goals have now won games, against Espanyol, Elche and Celta. He also scored in the 4-3 Champions League comeback win at Roma. The goal was his fourth of the season, the club said.

Recent findings suggest that espí called his first goal in front of the Bernabéu crowd his most special for the club. José Mourinho described him as a pure penalty-box striker. The coach added that football history has many players like him who decide games without playing many minutes.

Pablo Durán gave Celta a sixth-minute lead from a Williot Swedberg pass. Kylian Mbappé then missed a penalty in the 39th minute, and the visitors led 1-0 at the break.

It has been revealed that mourinho had started Vinícius and Federico Valverde on the bench. He sent them on with Marc Cucurella in the second half to chase the game. Thibaut Courtois kept Madrid in it with a strong low save from a long-range Durán shot in the 65th minute. A minute later, Jude Bellingham equalised from an Mbappé assist.

According to recent reports, the figures show how one-sided the contest was. Madrid had 24 shots to Celta’s 8 and an expected goals total of 3.8 against 1.52. Radu made five saves, and the hosts held 64% of possession.

Celta coach Claudio Giráldez said Madrid’s substitutes had decided the game. He pointed out that he had started six academy graduates. Many of his players were appearing at the Bernabéu for the first time. Giráldez replaced Hugo Álvarez with Ferran Jutglà at half-time and sent on Iago Aspas for Durán in the 76th minute. Celta are 13th on 13 points.

In a recent development, barcelona still top the table on goal difference, 35 to 22. They can move clear again when they host Villarreal on Sunday 22 November.

Recent findings suggest that in the LaLiga scoring chart, Mbappé is second with 13 goals. Barcelona’s Raphinha leads on 15.

📞 Just call Carlos Espí. #LaLigaHighlights pic.twitter.com/z9KqjfkhmY.

— Real Madrid C.F. 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@realmadriden) November 21, 2026.

Sources indicate that earlier on Saturday, Rafael Nadal was elected to Real Madrid’s board of directors at an Extraordinary General Assembly at Ciudad Real Madrid. Later, he watched the game from the stands and was visibly emotional.

Celta host Bournemouth in the Europa League at Balaídos on Thursday 26 November, with 3 points from four games. Madrid face PSV in the Champions League at the Bernabéu on Tuesday 24 November at 20:00 UTC. They have won all four of their league-phase games and sit second on 12 points, while PSV are 24th on 4 points.

Newcastle Unitedâs long wait for domestic silverware finally ended last season when they lifted the Carabao Cup â and the club marked the historic moment with a one-of-a-kind exhibition that captured the spirit of their journey to glory.

'The Road to Wembley', hosted at the Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art in collaboration with VERSUS, offered supporters an immersive, documentary-style retelling of the Magpiesâ cup success.

The exhibition featured more than 100 photographs by club photographers Serena Taylor, Harriet Massey and Michelle Mercer, each capturing intimate moments from the campaign. Visitors also experienced cinematic displays, installations from fan group Wor Flags, and the rare chance to stand alongside the Carabao Cup trophy itself.

The launch event included a panel featuring curators Ewen Spencer and Jimmy Turrell, alongside Newcastle legend Rob Lee, before celebrations spilled into the night with a DJ set.

The centrepiece of the story, of course, was Newcastleâs 2-1 victory over Liverpool in the final â sealed by Alexander Isakâs decisive strike.

With the Swede now not-so-subtly pining for a move to Liverpool, no less, the exhibition may have accidentally doubled up as his own farewell tour â a reminder that even if heroes donât always stick around, the memories (and the trophy) are here to stay.

Coady had also been helping out within his first club Liverpool's U21 set-up, prior to his deadline day departure from Wrexham.

He is keen to make the step up in club coaching and was linked with a role at Barnsley in recent weeks.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, julián Álvarez created both of Atlético Madrid's first-half goals as the visitors ended Getafe's unbeaten home league record this season.
  • Both of Atlético’s first-half goals in this matchday 13 LaLiga fixture came inside the opening 30 minutes.
  • Álex Baena opened the scoring in the 10th minute with a low, powerful shot from outside the area.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, julián Álvarez created both of Atlético Madrid's first-half goals as the visitors ended Getafe's unbeaten home league record this season. Atlético now sit two points behind Real Madrid, while Getafe are left one point above the relegation zone before the midweek European games.

Both of Atlético’s first-half goals in this matchday 13 LaLiga fixture came inside the opening 30 minutes.

Álex Baena opened the scoring in the 10th minute with a low, powerful shot from outside the area. It was his sixth LaLiga goal of the season. Johnny Cardoso doubled the lead on 30 minutes when David Soria missed a punch at a corner. It was Cardoso’s first league goal for Atlético.

Industry observers note that getafe finished with ten men. VAR confirmed a penalty involving Alexander Sørloth in the 89th minute. Dakonam Ortega Djené was then sent off in the 90th minute, having been booked in the 71st. Álex Grimaldo converted the penalty in the second minute of stoppage time for his fifth goal of the league campaign. About 10,000 spectators watched the game, according to Telemadrid.

The visitors had 68% of the ball and completed 652 accurate passes to Getafe’s 238. They took 20 shots to the hosts’ 11. Getafe’s goalkeeper made 7 saves, while Jan Oblak needed to make only 1.

Álvarez played 75 minutes and created 4 key passes. Baena was rated 8.2 and Cardoso 8.13. Diego Simeone was without Ademola Lookman, Marc Pubill and Cristian ‘Cuti’ Romero for the trip.

It has been revealed that the win followed two straight defeats for Atlético, 1-2 against Barcelona and 0-2 against Bayern München. It also followed last season’s 0-1 Atlético win at the Coliseum on 23 November 2025.

Barcelona lead the table on 36 points, with Real Madrid second on 33.

It has been revealed that pepe Bordalás’s side went into the game having lost every away league match without scoring. They had conceded 14 goals on the road.

#FINAL | Derrota.@GetafeCF 0⃣-3⃣ @Atleti #GetafeAtleti pic.twitter.com/lCpJZ8dHws.

Sources indicate that — Getafe C.F. (@GetafeCF) November 22, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that getafe have lost their last three games in all competitions, against Brighton, Villarreal and Atlético. They sit 17th with 12 points and a goal difference of -13. Levante are 18th on 11 points and Elche 19th on 10, both with a game in hand. Getafe could fall into the relegation zone if Levante or Elche win their games on Monday, VAVEL España reported.

In a recent development, atlético return to action on Wednesday 25 November against Viking at the Metropolitano. That game is matchday 5 of the Champions League league phase, and both sides have four points going into it. Getafe travel to FC Iberia 1999 in the UEFA Conference League on Thursday 26 November.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that female mosquitoes use several sensory systems to locate a host whose blood they can feed on. One of these systems is a group of proteins known as ionotropic receptors, which detect the acidic compounds in human sweat that contribute to its sour smell. Writing in Nature, Xu et al.1 report 3D structures of an ionotropic-receptor complex from the malaria-spreading mosquito Anopheles stephensi. The structures show how the binding of an acid activates the receptor, which then opens its ion-conducting pore and generates an electrical signal that helps to guide the mosquito towards a human host.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two headers from Cucho Hernández gave Real Betis victory over Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League. The result strengthens Manuel Pellegrini's side's position in the league phase with three rounds left.

In a recent development, for Hernández, Tuesday night was his first start after more than a month out injured, and he marked it with a double in Bratislava. The win came in the fifth round of the Champions League league stage.

According to recent reports, ángel Ortiz supplied the cross for the opener, delivering it from the right for Hernández to meet at the back post. Isco then supplied the assist for his second after the break. That goal was his third of Betis’s Champions League campaign.

Sources indicate that hernández went off after 63 minutes, and Troy Parrott took his place. Marc Roca replaced Facundo Bernal, who had been booked in the seventh minute. Álvaro Fidalgo came on for Isco.

Industry observers note that pellegrini made six changes from the side that drew 1-1 with Sevilla in the derby. Isco, Abde and Antony kept their places.

Recent findings suggest that the visitors dominated the game in every department. Betis completed 605 of their 670 passes, an accuracy of 90%. Slovan managed 309 passes in total. Betis put six shots on target, while Slovan managed two. The expected goals figure was 1.52 for Betis and 0.43 for the hosts.

In a recent development, slovan goalkeeper Dominik Takáč made four saves. At the other end, Álvaro Vallés made a sharp save to stop Andraž Šporar, a moment UEFA’s match summary named as one of the key moments of the game. French referee Jérôme Brisard showed one yellow card to each side.

The game also brought Slovan coach Yaya Touré up against Pellegrini, his old manager at Manchester City. Touré’s side stay bottom of the table after five defeats. They have conceded 19 goals and scored only one.

Industry observers note that betis now have four wins and one defeat from five matches. They are well placed to fight for a top-eight finish over the last three rounds, according to AFP. A place in the top eight would send them straight into the last 16 without a play-off.

Recent findings suggest that the remaining fixtures are demanding. Betis host Como on 9 December 2026 and Arsenal on 20 January 2027. They finish the league phase away to Bayern Munich on 27 January 2027.
